MSCI Drops Saylor's Strategy From Its Index Amid BTC Sell-Off

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read | Sumber: https://u.today/msci-drops-saylors-strategy-from-its-index-amid-btc-sell-off

💡 Key Takeaways
  • MSCI has published the results of its November 2026 Index Review, with Strategy among the companies set to leave the MSCI USA Index.
  • Metaplanet, the Tokyo-listed Bitcoin treasury organization, is also scheduled for removal from the MSCI Japan Small Cap Index.
  • The changes will take effect after the market close on November 30, 2026.

MSCI has published the results of its November 2026 Index Review, with Strategy among the companies set to leave the MSCI USA Index.

Metaplanet, the Tokyo-listed Bitcoin treasury organization, is also scheduled for removal from the MSCI Japan Small Cap Index.

The changes will take effect after the market close on November 30, 2026.

Across the MSCI ACWI Index, 13 securities will be added and 100 deleted. The two additions to the MSCI World Index, measured by full company market capitalization, are Moderna (USA) and Aritzia (Canada).

The latest review follows the newly introduced rules proposed by MSCI in October, among which are new measures regarding crypto treasury holding companies.

According to recent reports, MSCI evaluates whether a firm maintains substantial operating assets and applies five financial ratio tests. In case a company fails to meet at least four criteria,.

A company that fails at least four criteria across consecutive annual reporting periods may face removal from the MSCI Global Investable Market Indexes.

MSCI indexes track public companies based on market cap and investment risks. Global mutual funds and ETFs use these benchmarks to build their portfolios.

Dropping out of such index could influence investment flows as well as stock prices.

Strategy continues to accumulate BTC despite the crypto market staying in red zone.

Between November 2 and November 8, 2026, the tech giant acquired another 1,036 BTC at an average price of $79,012.

Recent findings suggest that as of November 12, Strategy holds 850,364 BTC. The organization also reported about $5.5 billion in USD reserves.

However, Bitcoin's recent decline below $75,000 pushes Strategy's holdings into an unrealized loss of $500 million.

Strategy's stock (MSTR) fell 7% on Thursday, while Bitcoin is down 3.5% at the time of writing.

Funds that track those indexes will have to sell their Strategy shares. JPMorgan earlier estimated that selling at about $2.8 billion. Strategy notes the funds hold about 13 million shares, 3.1% of its stock. Its shares are down 1.8% before the open.

For Bitcoin news, that matters beyond one stock. Strategy is the steadiest corporate buyer of Bitcoin. Fewer index buyers for its shares could make it harder and more costly to raise money for new purchases.

#210. Unocoin Suspends Withdrawals After Suspicious BitGo Wallet Transfers

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4 min read (770 words)
General

Unocoin Suspends Withdrawals After Suspicious BitGo Wallet Transfers

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read | Sumber: https://bitcoinist.com/unocoin-suspends-withdrawals-after-suspicious-bitgo-wallet-transfers/

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, indian cryptocurrency exchange Unocoin has maintained its suspension of deposits and withdrawals while investigating suspicious transactions involving its BitGo wallet infrastructure.
  • Unocoin said on November 13 that BitGo froze its enterprise account on November 6 at the exchange’s request and that the freeze operated as intended.
  • The latest development centers on a recovery feature included in BitGo’s multisignature wallet infrastructure.

According to recent reports, indian cryptocurrency exchange Unocoin has maintained its suspension of deposits and withdrawals while investigating suspicious transactions involving its BitGo wallet infrastructure. The latest update suggests that the transfers may have been executed through a recovery mechanism outside BitGo’s platform, raising newly introduced questions about how the activity occurred despite the custodian account being frozen.

Unocoin said on November 13 that BitGo froze its enterprise account on November 6 at the exchange’s request and that the freeze operated as intended. However, the transactions under investigation were reportedly signed and broadcast outside BitGo’s platform.

The latest development centers on a recovery feature included in BitGo’s multisignature wallet infrastructure. According to Unocoin, this mechanism allows wallet holders to access their assets if BitGo becomes unavailable.

The exchange suspects that the feature may have been misused to authorize transactions outside the custodian’s regular platform. This could explain how outgoing transfers were possible even after BitGo confirmed that its enterprise account had been frozen.

Unocoin previously disclosed that it identified outgoing transactions from an Ethereum address within its BitGo wallet infrastructure on November 12. The address was used to fund ERC-20 tokens, and the exchange immediately escalated the matter to BitGo.

The custodian subsequently opened an investigation into how the transfers were executed. Unocoin’s latest explanation provides a possible avenue for investigators to examine, but it has not confirmed that the recovery feature was exploited or established who authorized the transactions.

The incident began on November 6, when Unocoin detected unauthorized activity within its infrastructure. The exchange responded by requesting immediate freezes of its enterprise accounts with BitGo and Fireblocks, which hold cryptocurrency balances used for its daily operations.

Both providers confirmed the freezes. Unocoin mentioned that, at the time, it had not identified any loss of cryptocurrency funds.

However, further unauthorized activity was detected on November 9. The exchange then suspended all services as a precautionary measure to protect customer assets and information.

In a recent development, its subsequent investigation established that its infrastructure had been compromised. The manufacturer has not yet identified the precise cause of the breach or determined which systems and information may have been exposed.

According to recent reports, unocoin also decided to rebuild its entire server infrastructure rather than attempt to restore the potentially compromised environment. Its November 12 security revision estimated that the process would require approximately four to five working days.

Unocoin has emphasized that more than 90% of the cryptocurrency it holds on behalf of customers is maintained in cold storage, meaning the assets are kept in offline wallets.

Nevertheless, the exchange has not provided a definitive assessment of the funds potentially affected by the suspicious transfers.

Its investigation is complicated by the fact that its BitGo enterprise accounts remain frozen, preventing the company from accessing them directly. Unocoin has also pointed to BitGo’s use of change addresses, which can make it difficult to establish the complete transaction history through publicly available blockchain information.

As a result, the exchange claims it does not yet have full visibility into potentially unintended transfers across its BitGo wallets. It has requested transaction-level information and further clarification from the custodian.

The firm has stressed that it will not provide assurances about the status of customer holdings until the relevant information has been verified.

The incident highlights the security challenges associated with cryptocurrency custody arrangements, particularly when recovery mechanisms provide alternative ways to access wallet funds.

According to recent reports, multisignature wallets are commonly used to strengthen asset protection by requiring multiple approvals before transactions can be completed. However, recovery procedures and backup mechanisms also need to be secured because they can create additional pathways for accessing funds.

Unocoin’s investigation is now focused on determining how the transactions were authorized, whether its wallet recovery infrastructure was involved, and whether any customer assets were affected.

Ethereum’s [ETH] staking ratio has reportedly reached an all-time high (ATH)  of 36.3%, accounting for more than one-third of ETH’s total circulating supply. Well, the rising staking ratio suggests that an increasing number of ETH holders are choosing to lock up their tokens rather than sell or actively trade them.

According to recent reports, this comes as Ethereum’s validator queues show that at press time, 911,938 ETH was waiting to be staked with a 16-day, 7-hour wait. Meanwhile, 264,211 ETH was queued to exit with a 5-day, 16-hour wait, plus a 7-day sweep delay.

Both queues are limited by the same churn rate of 256 per epoch, meaning only a fixed amount of ETH can join or leave each epoch, which is why a significant backlog translates into longer waits.

In other words, more people want to stake than unstake right now, but the entry line is slowly shrinking, and exiting takes roughly 12-13 days in total once the sweep delay is included.

This comes as the total ETH staked rose from about 42.1 million ETH (roughly 34.5% of supply) in mid-August to about 44.5 million ETH (around 36.5%) at press time. Since late October the climb has resumed steadily.

Of this, BitMine earned $121.4 million from staking and validation activities, accounting for approximately 97% of its total revenue. By the 8th of November, the largest Ethereum DAT held 6.07 million ETH, of which 5.22 million ETH was staked.

That mentioned, the manufacturer also estimates that these holdings could generate around $309 million in annual staking rewards, based on an estimated 2.65% yield and an ETH price of $2,234.

On the other hand, SharpLink has accumulated 31,363 ETH in staking rewards as of 9th November. Its strategy also includes liquid staking through Lido, allowing it to receive wstETH in return for its deposited ETH.

Recent findings suggest that all of this happened while the active validators moved in the opposite direction. As per charts, they held near 900K through mid-September, peaking around 912K. But again, they dropped sharply from mid-September to mid-October, falling to about 815K, and have since drifted down to roughly 807K, with a small additional drop on the last day or two.

It has been revealed that however, the price action of ETH trading at $2,042.94 at press time after a modest drop in the past 24 hours but a 15.5% drop in the past week sparks concern. This comes as Ethereum faces renewed selling pressure after losing its $2,250 support level. However, Vitalik Buterin’s recent push to position ETH as a store of value suggests hope.

Decentralized exchange Hyperliquid has bought back and burned 21,200 HYPE over the past 24 hours, spending $1.53 million on the purchase at an average price of $72.31, according to Onchain Lens.

According to recent reports, the on-chain analytics platform also reported that Hyperliquid has permanently removed a total of 50.47 million HYPE from circulation since the launch of the token. That is 5.05% of the max supply of 1 billion HYPE, and at the current price, the burned tokens are worth around $3.51 billion.

It has been revealed that the latest buyback comes amid the decline in the price of the cryptocurrency. On Nov. 12, the price of HYPE went down by 3.45%, and at press time, the token stands at $69.52, according to TradingView. Earlier this autumn, the price of HYPE was above $90.

Hyperliquid pays for the buybacks in dollars, so the decentralized exchange is able to buy more HYPE with the same amount of money when the price of the token goes down.

DeFiLlama data demonstrates that Hyperliquid has earned $1.41 billion for HYPE holders since December 2024. Over the past 30 days, the decentralized exchange earned $68.82 million, and its earnings for the past week stand at $15.04 million.

Over the last day, the platform collected about $1.46 million in fees, slightly less than the amount it spent on the buyback. Besides, DeFiLlama data indicates that Hyperliquid currently earns more in fees than Ethereum, Tron and Base.

The largest part of the burned tokens, 48.85 million HYPE, was bought back by the Assistance Fund. The fund automatically receives between 97% and 99% of the fees from perpetual and spot trading on Hyperliquid, and the rest of the fees go to the HLP liquidity pool and to the builders of individual markets.

Sources indicate that the Assistance Fund buys HYPE on the open market and sends the tokens to the "0xfefe...fefe" address. It is a system address that does not have a private key. In December 2025, Hyperliquid validators formally recognized the tokens held at this address as burned.

It has been revealed that in August 2026, Hyperliquid also introduced the AQAv2 upgrade. Under the upgrade, around 90% of the yield generated by the USDC reserves on the platform now goes to the Assistance Fund. Each of these transfers brings between $14 million and $16 million to the fund.

It has been revealed that besides the Assistance Fund, HYPE is also burned through network fees. Around 1.24 million HYPE has been burned through fees and slashing on HyperCore, the base layer of Hyperliquid. Another 376,060 HYPE has been burned as gas fees on HyperEVM, the smart contract layer of the network.

Trump nominates Hester Peirce successor among SEC, CFTC picks

  • According to recent reports, the White House’s latest announcement on Thursday named two nominees each for the SEC and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, agencies whose decisions help shape US cryptocurrency regulation, among other functions.

The White House also named a former CFTC commissioner and two CLARITY Act veterans as nominees to fill vacancies at the SEC and CFTC.

US President Donald Trump has nominated Steven Levine to replace former Securities and Exchange Commission Commissioner Hester Peirce, one of the agency’s most prominent crypto advocates, as part of four nominations to fill vacancies at the SEC and Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

According to recent reports, the White House’s latest announcement on Thursday named two nominees each for the SEC and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, agencies whose decisions help shape US cryptocurrency regulation, among other functions. All four nominations require Senate confirmation.

Sources indicate that the nominations would replenish several commissioner roles. The SEC at the moment has only two of its five commissioner seats filled, while CFTC Chairman Michael Selig is the sole member of his agency’s five-seat commission.

The nominations come weeks before Democrats are set to take control of the Senate in January, giving a narrow window for Republicans to confirm Trump’s picks.

Related: House Finance panel chair says regulator actions on crypto ‘fall short’ of CLARITY bill.

Recent findings suggest that levine, a Republican, was nominated for an SEC term ending June 5, 2030, replacing Peirce, who left the agency in October. Peirce was a leading advocate for clearer crypto rules at the SEC, helping shape its approach to digital assets as the former head of its Crypto Task Force, while Levine’s views on crypto regulation are less publicly established.

Trump also nominated Democrat Kristin Johnson, a former CFTC commissioner, for the SEC seat held by Caroline Crenshaw, whose term has also expired. Johnson’s proposed term ends June 5, 2029. Johnson has advocated for stronger customer protections and conflict-of-interest rules for crypto firms in her time at the CFTC.

According to recent reports, for the CFTC, Trump nominated Republican Nathan Anonick and Democrat Matthew Rowland, both of whom worked on the Clarity Act. CFTC Chairman Mike Selig called them “two strong bipartisan picks” for CFTC commissioners and said he looked forward to working with them upon their confirmation.

The nominees would typically appear before the Senate Banking Committee for the SEC positions and the Senate Agriculture Committee for the CFTC roles. Following committee consideration, their nominations would go to the full Senate, where confirmation requires a majority vote.

Strategy Made $19.5 Billion in Profit. So Why Is MSCI Removing It From Stock Indexes?

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read | Sumber: https://decrypt.co/383204/why-msci-removing-bitcoin-treasury-strategy-stock-indexes

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, strategy Made $19.5 Billion in Profit.
  • Strategy made $19.53 billion in profit last quarter.
  • Industry observers note that MSCI’s November review lists “STRATEGY A”—the firm’s MSTR shares—for deletion from the MSCI USA Index after trading closes November 30.

According to recent reports, strategy Made $19.5 Billion in Profit. So Why Is MSCI Removing It From Stock Indexes?

Strategy made $19.53 billion in profit last quarter. Yet MSCI, one of the world’s biggest providers of stock indexes, has decided Michael Saylor’s Bitcoin company no longer belongs in some of its major investment benchmarks.

Industry observers note that MSCI’s November review lists “STRATEGY A”—the firm’s MSTR shares—for deletion from the MSCI USA Index after trading closes November 30. That also removes the stock from broader indexes that include U.S. companies, such as the MSCI World and MSCI All Country World indexes.

Industry observers note that that sounds technical, but the distinction matters: MSCI is not removing Strategy from the Nasdaq stock exchange, shutting down its business, or making it sell Bitcoin. It is taking MSTR out of stock lists that investment funds use to decide which companies to own.

Consider an ETF designed to copy the MSCI USA Index. When MSTR disappears from the list, the fund generally has to sell its shares, regardless of whether the fund manager likes Saylor’s strategy.

This is why it’s bad news for Strategy. It means less indirect exposition to investments.

Sources indicate that MSCI adopted new rules in October for so-called non-operating companies. The idea is to keep investment vehicles—businesses that mainly hold financial assets—out of indexes meant to track operating companies. Its screening process considers a manufacturer’s operating assets and other financial measures.

According to recent reports, MSCI’s deletion list does not spell out exactly which tests Strategy failed. The organization, however, argues that raising capital, managing its Bitcoin treasury and issuing financial products amount to a genuine operating business.

In an August letter to MSCI, Strategy called the proposal “discriminatory, arbitrary, and misguided.” It argued that MSCI should be a “mirror of the market, not an arbiter of it.”.

Industry observers note that strategy also maintains a software business, but Bitcoin now dominates its finances. The disagreement is whether its Bitcoin activity counts as running a tech giant or mainly managing an investment portfolio.

Strategy’s latest quarterly earnings show $19.53 billion in net income. But that does not mean its software customers paid the tech giant anything close to that amount.

Nearly all of its $20.91 billion in reported operating income came from a rise in the accounting value of its Bitcoin. Under rules adopted in 2025, changes in Bitcoin’s market price appear in Strategy’s earnings even when it has not sold the coins. A decline in Bitcoin can produce the opposite result.

According to recent reports, its software division, meanwhile, recorded $125.4 million in quarterly revenue, down 3% from a year earlier. Its $477.2 million in revenue for all of 2025 was slightly below the $486.3 million reported in 2019, before Strategy began buying Bitcoin.

According to recent reports, the immediate risk is selling pressure on MSTR, not on Bitcoin itself. Strategy estimated that funds linked to MSCI indexes hold roughly 13 million of its shares, or 3.1% of its outstanding common stock. Not all of that necessarily translates into sudden sales, and Strategy claims the amount is manageable.

Industry observers note that but Strategy has repeatedly raised money by selling shares and other securities, then used those proceeds to buy Bitcoin. If its stock falls, selling the same number of new shares brings in less cash.

So the company would have to issue more shares to raise the same amount—or buy fewer Bitcoin.

That is why a stock-index decision could eventually matter to the crypto market. The exclusion does not force a Bitcoin sale, and it does not guarantee fewer purchases. It could, however, weaken a key source of funding for one of Bitcoin’s biggest corporate buyers.

The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC) will connect its tokenization service to Solana (SOL) in the second half of 2027, the company mentioned on Nov. 12.

It has been revealed that the integration will allow "digital twins" of Russell 1000 stocks, major ETFs and U.S. Treasuries to be issued on the Solana blockchain. In December 2025, the SEC issued a no-action letter that allowed DTC to tokenize these assets.

According to recent reports, in 2025, DTCC processed $4.7 quadrillion in securities transactions. Its depository, DTC, holds and services $114 trillion in assets from more than 150 countries.

The DTCC Tokenization Service (DTS) will let large market participants convert conventional securities into tokens, move them across the Solana network and redeem them.

"DTC-tokenized assets made available on Solana – and all blockchain networks integrated with the service – will retain the same investor protections, ownership rights and regulatory safeguards that apply to traditionally held securities," mentioned Brian Steele, president of DTCC Clearing & Securities Services.

According to DTCC CEO Frank La Salla, the integration will also free up securities for use as collateral.

It has been revealed that DTS went live on Oct. 28, 2026. At launch, it worked with Canton Network and a private ledger. DTCC noted that it adds new networks at clients' request.

"DTCC is committed to providing an open and connected platform that provides our users with access to mature distributed ledger technology networks like Solana that have established performance, security and governance features," remarked Nadine Chakar, global head of DTCC Digital Assets.

According to recent reports, nick Ducoff, general manager for institutional at the Solana Foundation, also commented on the news. "Institutions choose Solana because it already runs real financial activity at scale," he noted.

According to Ducoff, the integration "connects one of the most trusted names in post-trade infrastructure with a network built for always-on markets.".

Sources indicate that as of Nov. 12, distributed real-world assets (RWA) in the Solana ecosystem reached $5.13 billion across more than 1.02 million holders, according to RWA.xyz. Transfers over the past 30 days totaled $16.48 billion.

The stablecoin market cap on Solana stands at $13.85 billion, with monthly turnover of $387.41 billion.

Sources indicate that the Zcash [ZEC] community is gearing up to vote on a proposal that could significantly change how ZEC funds its development and distributes newly created tokens. The plan involves removing 50,000 ZEC from the Zcash Community Grants (ZCG) treasury and redirecting its value toward future mining rewards.

That said, Zcash right now allocates 8% of newly issued ZEC to ZCG, which uses the funds to support developers, wallet providers, and other ecosystem projects.

Industry observers note that these grants help maintain the infrastructure and software needed to use ZEC. However, rising ZEC prices has increased the value of ZCG’s existing treasury, which has raised concerns that the committee was accumulating more funds than necessary while continuing to receive latest token allocations.

However, now, under the new proposal, approximately 55% of ZCG’s treasury (50,000 ZEC) would be removed from circulation within 30 days of activation. Going ahead, its value would be credited to the Network Sustainability Mechanism, introduced through the NU7 upgrade. This, in turn, would gradually return ZEC to the network through future mining rewards.

At the same time, the proposal would also end ZCG’s existing 8% allocation of newly created ZEC. Instead, this share would accumulate in a upcoming Future Dev and Legal Defense Fund until the next halving takes place.

According to recent reports, as this happens, the fund would remain inaccessible until a separate proposal establishes withdrawal rules. Lastly, ZCG would retain its remaining treasury to continue funding development, while the separate 12% Coinholder-Controlled Fund would remain unchanged.

For those unaware, the revised proposal follows ZCG’s 3rd November decision to abandon an earlier proposal, which faced criticism for seeking to redirect approximately 98,000 ZEC from existing assets and future income toward mining rewards.

It has been revealed that so, now, the next step is community voting, which is scheduled from 16th November to 30th November. Coinholders and community panels will assess the proposal’s support.

If it receives rough consensus, developers, and miners can work toward implementing it through a future network upgrade called NU7.1. However, there is no confirmed activation date yet.

This coincided with Zcash’s monthly active developer count having nearly doubled over the past two years.

According to Glassnode’s report, around 70% of its active developers have more than one year of experience in crypto development, compared with 58% across the wider industry.

#225. Western Europe’s Crypto Economy Reaches $2.08T as Stablecoin Holdings Surge 131%

Western Europe’s Crypto Economy Reaches $2.08T as Stablecoin Holdings Surge 131%

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read | Sumber: https://bitcoinist.com/western-europes-crypto-economy-reaches-2-08t-as-stablecoin-holdings-surge-131/

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Western Europe’s crypto economy continued to expand despite a broader global market downturn, reaching $2.08 trillion in annual transaction activity as stablecoin adoption accelerated across the region.
  • Sources indicate that A report published by blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis on November 9 found that crypto activity increased 1.2% between July 2025 and June 2026.
  • Recent findings suggest that stablecoins were one of the strongest areas of expansion.

Western Europe’s crypto economy continued to expand despite a broader global market downturn, reaching $2.08 trillion in annual transaction activity as stablecoin adoption accelerated across the region.

Sources indicate that A report published by blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis on November 9 found that crypto activity increased 1.2% between July 2025 and June 2026. This made Western Europe the world’s second-largest regional crypto economy and placed it among only three regions to record positive growth during the period.

Recent findings suggest that stablecoins were one of the strongest areas of expansion. Holdings in personal wallets across Western Europe climbed 131%, significantly outperforming the global growth rate of 52%. However, the figures also revealed contrasting trends among major markets, with the UK retaining its position as Europe’s largest crypto economy despite an annual decline in overall activity.

Industry observers note that the UK accounted for the largest share of Western Europe’s cryptocurrency activity, recording approximately $424.5 billion in transaction value during the reporting period. Nevertheless, activity declined 8% year over year, with reduced decentralized exchange trading contributing to the slowdown.

Germany ranked second with $288.8 billion, followed by France at $215.8 billion and the Netherlands at $207.8 billion. Spain and Switzerland recorded $156.1 billion and $132.8 billion, respectively.

Together, these six countries represented roughly two-thirds of the region’s total crypto economy, highlighting how heavily activity remains concentrated in Western Europe’s largest financial markets.

Stablecoins emerged as one of the most significant drivers of Western Europe’s crypto expansion. Personal-wallet holdings increased by 131% over the 12-month reporting period, compared with 52% growth worldwide.

It has been revealed that the region’s share of global stablecoin balances consequently increased from 3.4% to 5.1%. Austria and France recorded particularly strong gains, while the broader trend suggests that stablecoins are becoming more important to how Europeans store and move digital assets.

Regulatory developments are also shaping the market. The European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) has established a common framework for crypto-asset issuers and service providers, creating clearer requirements for businesses operating across the bloc.

Despite the contraction in its overall crypto economy, the UK recorded a substantial increase in domestic stablecoin activity.

Transfers between UK-based wallets reached $2.09 billion during the reporting period, compared with just $109 million in the previous 12 months. This represented approximately 60% of Western Europe’s total domestic stablecoin transfer value, exceeding the combined $1.41 billion recorded across the rest of the region.

Sources indicate that the findings suggest that stablecoins are increasingly being used for domestic transactions rather than exclusively for international transfers. In the UK, domestic stablecoin transfers were 1.32 times the value of the cross-border activity measured by Chainalysis. The rest of Western Europe displayed the opposite pattern, with cross-border transfers significantly outweighing domestic activity.

Retail wallet behavior also reflected growing interest in stablecoins. Approximately 1.03% of eligible UK retail wallets converted at least 80% of their cryptocurrency holdings into stablecoins, up from 0.66% a year earlier.

France recorded another notable development, with stablecoin balances held in personal wallets increasing by 192% during the reporting period.

In a recent development, the number of French personal wallets holding stablecoins rose from 3,577 in June 2025 to 12,255 in June 2026. Stablecoins also accounted for 54.2% of withdrawals from centralized exchanges by the end of the period, the highest proportion among the major Western European markets included in the analysis.

The trend unfolded amid fiscal pressure and political uncertainty in France. Chainalysis noted that the growth in self-custody coincided with periods of stress in the country’s bond market, although the data does not establish a direct causal relationship.

The increase suggests that more French crypto consumers are choosing to move stablecoins away from centralized platforms and hold them in personal wallets. This gives users greater direct control over their digital assets while reflecting a broader shift in how stablecoins are used across the region.

It has been revealed that western Europe’s $2.08 trillion crypto economy demonstrates that the region has maintained growth even as global market conditions weakened. However, the report demonstrates that this expansion is not uniform.

Sources indicate that the UK remains the largest market by transaction value, but its annual contraction contrasts with the growth recorded in other parts of the region. Meanwhile, stablecoin holdings, domestic transfers, and self-custody are becoming increasingly important indicators of how European customers interact with digital assets.

MiCA’s regulatory framework could further influence this development by providing clearer requirements for businesses and encouraging traditional financial institutions to explore blockchain-based services. At the same time, the expansion of euro-denominated stablecoins may strengthen the connection between conventional finance and digital asset markets.

Whether these trends translate into sustained growth will depend on regulatory implementation, institutional participation, and continued demand for stablecoin-based financial services.

Bank of America (BofA) says hot CPI puts a 50bps December Fed hike on the table. BTC fell a week later after 5 of the last 6 big hikes.

Bank of America said this week that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates by half a percentage point in December. The warning came after Tuesday’s October inflation report ran hotter than expected for a third month in a row. In Bitcoin news, the coin trades at $73,888 on Binance, down 0.6% in 24 hours. It dropped to $72,727 on Tuesday after the report, its lowest price since August 20.

Recent findings suggest that the bank still expects the Fed to raise rates by 0.25 percentage points, or 25 basis points (bps), at its December 8–9 meeting. But it says the case for a bigger move is growing, and it calls the Fed’s decision to hold rates in October a possible policy mistake.

According to recent reports, traders are starting to listen. On Polymarket, the odds of a hike of 50 bps or more in December rose from 0.6% on Monday to 11.4% on Wednesday.

BANK OF AMERICA WARNS FED COULD DELIVER 50BPS HIKE IN DECEMBER.

Bank of America says October's hot CPI report virtually guarantees a December Fed rate hike — and opens the door to a larger 50bps move.

Headline CPI rose 0.4%, while core CPI climbed 0.3%, marking a third….

— *Walter Bloomberg (@DeItaone) November 11, 2026.

The bank’s call rests on three months of hot data. Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, and core prices, which leave out food and energy because they swing the most, rose 0.3%. Both beat forecasts, the third upside surprise in a row in the Bureau of Labor Statistics report.

Bank of America now estimates that core PCE inflation, the Fed’s preferred measure, is running at 3.3% a year. The Fed’s target is 2%. The bank says price rises are spreading from goods to services, with electronics, airfares and hotels leading the increases.

According to recent reports, its base case is still a 25 bps hike in December. The change is in the risks: a 50 bps move is now possible, and the bank sees a growing chance of another hike in January instead of March.

The bank is not alone. Fed Governor Christopher Waller mentioned in a speech on Tuesday morning that he leans toward a 25 bps hike in December. If core inflation came in around 0.3% again, he said, a 50 bps hike “should be considered.” It did.

It has been revealed that higher rates make cash and bonds pay more. That tends to pull money out of risky assets like BTC, and a faster pace of hikes pulls harder.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Newly introduced Crypto to Hodl.

The size of the hike has mattered for BTC. We measured Bitcoin’s price on Binance from the 2 p.m. ET announcement of each Fed rate hike since 2022 to one week later. That covers 12 hikes: six of 50 bps or more and six of 25 bps.

It has been revealed that after the six big hikes, BTC was lower a week later five times. The median move was a 6% drop. The worst came after the 50 bps hike in May 2022, when BTC fell 23% in a week.

After the six 25 bps hikes, the picture was milder. BTC was lower a week later four times, but the median move was a drop of just 0.6%.

The record comes with a caveat. All six big hikes happened in 2022, a bear market that also saw the collapses of Terra in May and FTX in November. Those crashes made the falls after the May and November hikes worse.

The most recent hike was a 25 bps move on September 16. BTC rose 11.3% in the week after it, as the uncertainty that had built up before the meeting cleared. That makes the size of December’s hike, more than the hike itself, the Bitcoin news to watch.

DISCOVER: Bitcoin CPI Reaction: 10 of 13 Cool Inflation Reports Triggered an Hourly Gain – Can Inflation Data Reverse the Downtrend?

BTC trades at $73,888, down 0.6% in 24 hours and 5.8% over the past week. It sits below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that give recent prices more weight, on the daily chart. The 50-day EMA stands at $78,897 and the 200-day EMA at $76,449.

For Bitcoin news, the next test is the Fed’s own message. Traders already expect a 25 bps hike. If more officials join Waller and Bank of America in backing 50 bps, BTC may have to defend $72,727 before the December 9 decision.

#230. Why the Path to Quantum Resistance Runs Uphill for Bitcoin Wallet Makers

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3 min read (659 words)
General

Why the Path to Quantum Resistance Runs Uphill for Bitcoin Wallet Makers

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read | Sumber: https://decrypt.co/383201/why-path-quantum-resistance-runs-uphill-bitcoin-wallet

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Why the Path to Quantum Resistance Runs Uphill for Bitcoin Wallet Makers.
  • Bitcoin custody has always involved some degree of risk, but wallet manufacturers like Trezor—which build physical devices designed to keep a user’s private keys secure offline—are preparing for a post-quantum world where upcoming challenges arise.
  • That’s because SHRINCS, the community’s leading candidate for a post-quantum signature scheme, allows people to make transactions using stateful signatures that require rigid state tracking to prevent funds from being stolen, according to Trezor CTO Tomáš Sušánka.

Why the Path to Quantum Resistance Runs Uphill for Bitcoin Wallet Makers.

Bitcoin custody has always involved some degree of risk, but wallet manufacturers like Trezor—which build physical devices designed to keep a user’s private keys secure offline—are preparing for a post-quantum world where upcoming challenges arise.

That’s because SHRINCS, the community’s leading candidate for a post-quantum signature scheme, allows people to make transactions using stateful signatures that require rigid state tracking to prevent funds from being stolen, according to Trezor CTO Tomáš Sušánka.

Proposed late last year by Blockstream Research Director Jonas Nick and cryptographer Mikhail Kudinov, SHRINCS centers on a composite hash-based approach: people can make transactions using either stateful signatures or stateless signatures.

Stateless signatures are quite large—potentially affecting fees, signature speed, and other efficiency metrics—but are safe to reuse, while smaller, more efficient stateful signatures come with serious security risks when reused beyond a particular signing budget.

The stateful component of SHRINCS is made up of a tree of one-time signatures, and if these keys are accidentally used more than once, enough cryptographic information is revealed for someone else to forge that user’s signature and effectively steal funds.

If Bitcoin successfully adopts SHRINCS, maintaining a meticulous count of the wallet’s state will become a critical responsibility for wallet developers—with lots of potential edge-case security risks.

In a recent development, “You’re giving them an option to mess up,” Sušánka said during a recent episode of MARA Foundation TV, in reference to state tracking. “It’s our job to make it in a secure way, right? It shouldn't be the user’s job.”.

In a recent development, to mitigate this risk, Trezor is weighing options for how to support secure UX in a post-quantum world. For instance, Sušánka remarked the company is considering making the heavier, slower stateless signatures the default setting for all people, tucking the riskier stateful option behind an advanced settings wall.

While Sušánka recognizes that SHRINCS may be the conservative cryptographic choice because it relies on the same cryptographic assumptions as SHA-256, he is “kind of torn on the topic because maintaining the state is a burden.”.

Industry observers note that “For example, you can have two Trezors with the same recovery seed. How do you share the state between those two? You really don’t,” he added.

“That being said, as it is with everything, this is about trade-offs,” Sušánka continued. “The [stateful] signatures are 10 times smaller ... That makes a big difference. So, I just don't want to throw it off the table completely.”.

According to recent reports, sušánka went on to share that while many are focused on Bitcoin’s migration path to post-quantum addresses and signatures, hardware wallet devices will also need to be physically updated for full quantum protection. Most signing devices use quantum-vulnerable cryptography for hardware-specific security functions, like firmware and device authentication.

If people want to ensure their devices are secure in a post-quantum world, they will need to use “quantum-ready” devices—that is, devices that use post-quantum cryptography for device and firmware authentication as well.

In anticipation of these needs, the company is already shipping products like Trezor Safe 7 that support post-quantum cryptography for wallet authentication processes. Of course, transactions made on these devices will only be quantum-secure once Bitcoin itself upgrades to post-quantum security.

That noted, Sušánka warned developers not to wait too long to give consumers migration options, as he believes the migration of potentially millions of users will take time.

“People should be ready to make compromises,” Sušánka stated. “If we’re all going to be very strict on what can and cannot be done, we’re not going to get anywhere.”.

It has been revealed that andré Beganski is a Senior Content Manager at MARA Foundation, producing content on topics including the intersection of quantum computing and cryptography. He has previously worked for Decrypt.

Sources indicate that on Nov. 5, with ether trading near $2,400, Wang sold 6,200 wrapped staked ETH (wstETH) for $18.5 million in USDC. Wrapped staked ETH is a version of Lido's staked ether (stETH) that can be used in DeFi protocols.

This week, ether traded about 14% lower than on the day of the sale, and Wang started buying it back.

He withdrew 5,246 ETH from Binance hot wallets in two transfers of 3,996 ETH and 1,250 ETH. The purchase cost him $10.78 million, so about $7.7 million from the Nov. 5 sale is still left in USDC, according to Lookonchain.

Wang then sent 3,996 ETH ($8.23 million) to Lido. Lido is the largest liquid staking protocol on Ethereum. He deposited the wstETH he received into Spark, a lending protocol in the Sky ecosystem, which was previously known as MakerDAO. In Spark, wstETH can be used as collateral, while it continues to earn staking rewards.

He started out arbitraging Bitcoin between overseas exchanges and China's Taobao and later co-founded F2Pool. He released the pool in 2013 together with Mao Shixing. At that time, F2Pool was one of the first Bitcoin mining pools in China.

It has been revealed that in 2015, he bought a condo in Pattaya for 2,900 BTC. He later sold it for 7 BTC, as the price of Bitcoin had risen many times over.

In 2025, Wang also funded and commanded Fram2, the first crewed spaceflight over Earth's polar regions, on a SpaceX Crew Dragon.

F2Pool also mined ether until Ethereum moved to proof-of-stake in September 2022. Before that, Wang introduced the non-custodial staking service stakefish. According to Wang, he decided to do it after a conversation with Vitalik Buterin in 2017. Stakefish was also one of the first node operators of Lido.

Ether is down more than 15% since the start of the month amid outflows from spot ETFs, according to SoSoValue. At press time, ETH is trading at $2,020.

Maple Finance co-founder Joe Flanagan and COO Ryan O’Shea are leaving over disagreements about the firm’s direction as SYRUP falls despite revenue growth.

Two senior executives are leaving onchain asset manager Maple Finance over disagreements about the firm’s direction as its SYRUP token slid more than 7% Thursday.

Maple co-founder and executive chairman Joe Flanagan noted Wednesday he would leave after seven years at the firm, describing a growing divide with fellow co-founder and CEO Sidney Powell.

“Over time, our views on strategy, leadership, and life have moved further apart,” Flanagan wrote. “I believe Maple is best served by one co-founder leading it forward from here.”.

Industry observers note that chief operating officer Ryan O’Shea also noted in a Thursday post on X that he would leave after nearly five years at Maple. “I’ll be stepping down as COO. I’ve come to a different view on the direction Maple should take, and I’ve decided it’s time to step aside,” he wrote.

SYRUP traded at $0.12 at 10:36 p.m. UTC Thursday, down 7.5% over 24 hours and 12% over the past week, according to CoinGecko. The token had a market capitalization of about $145 million.

Maple and Powell did not respond to Cointelegraph’s requests for comment by publication.

In a recent development, in a statement published Wednesday, Maple confirmed that Flanagan was stepping down as chairman and leaving the company. “This is an agreed and orderly transition,” the company stated, adding that his responsibilities would move to Powell and Maple’s existing leadership team.

The company did not announce a replacement chairman or specify how the departing executives’ duties would be carried out.

Industry observers note that flanagan remarked his differences with Powell reached a point where they were no longer constructive. “I am choosing to leave rather than continue supporting a direction I cannot stand behind,” he said. Flanagan added that he would help with the transition through the end of 2026.

O’Shea is stepping down effective Nov. 27. “I’ll have no ongoing role after that,” he wrote.

The departures come as Maple looks to expand beyond crypto-backed lending. In October, Powell stated the firm planned to reach more customers through fintech partnerships and lend against a wider range of assets, including payments owed on loans made by fintech companies and securities backed by assets such as mortgages.

Related: Kraken, Maple launch onchain warehouse facility for crypto-backed institutional loans.

The announcements come as Maple’s lending business continues to grow, while SYRUP is down 62% year to date and total value locked (TVL) has declined.

It has been revealed that according to Token Terminal, Maple’s protocol revenue rose 8% year over year in October, while TVL fell around 11% between the end of September and Nov. 11.

Maple’s latest quarterly results also indicated growth, with the organization reporting $4.4 million in third-quarter revenue, up 5% from a year earlier. Assets under management rose 18% year over year to $4.7 billion.

Industry observers note that maple has also been using some of its revenue to buy back SYRUP tokens. In September, the tech giant repurchased about 1.37 million tokens, twice as many as in August, according to its October update.

Why is crypto crashing on Wednesday, November 11? The sell-off that began with Tuesday’s hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation report has carried into today, and almost every major coin is lower.

Industry observers note that bitcoin (BTC) dropped below $73,000 on Tuesday, touching $72,727 on Binance, and now trades at about $73,800. Ether (ETH) briefly slipped to $2,006, while XRP and Solana (SOL) are down 2% to 3% in 24 hours. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, a daily gauge of market mood from 0 to 100, has fallen to 29.

The report changed what traders expect from the Federal Reserve. Bond yields jumped, and bets on a larger December rate hike nearly tripled within two hours.

One coin is falling much harder than the rest. Zcash (ZEC) is a cryptocurrency introduced in 2016 that lets users hide the sender, the receiver and the amount of a payment. It dropped below $1,000 on Wednesday for the first time since September 5. ZEC now trades at about $966, down 15.4% in 24 hours and 24.8% in a week.

ZEC has been one of this year’s best performers. It rose from about $526 on January 1 to a closing high of $1,653 on September 26. We checked the 20 largest coins on Binance, and ZEC fell the most over both the day and the week, even though it is still up 89% in 2026.

So why are the markets spooked, and why is ZEC taking the hardest hit?

It has been revealed that inflation came in hot. The consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% economists expected. Core prices, which leave out food and energy, rose 0.3% against a 0.2% forecast.

According to recent reports, that reading crossed a line the Fed had drawn. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech hours before the report that core inflation of about 0.3% would make a half-point hike in December worth considering.

Recent findings suggest that traders took him at his word. On Polymarket, the odds of a hike of 0.5 percentage point or more in December went from 4.4% just before the report to 12.8% two hours later. They sit at 9.4% now, while a standard quarter-point hike is priced at 85.5%.

Recent findings suggest that higher rates hurt crypto in a simple way. They make cash and bonds pay more, so money flows out of riskier bets. On Tuesday, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield rose from 4.86% to 4.98%.

It has been revealed that ZEC had the most to give back. We compared the price changes of 20 large coins on Binance over the past week and since January 1.

According to recent reports, when markets get nervous, traders tend to sell what has made them the most money. ZEC has fallen 41% from its September 26 closing high of $1,653.

Borrowed money made the drop faster. On Hyperliquid, ZEC fell from $1,199.20 to $965.79 in less than a day. Lookonchain counted 32 traders holding more than $1 million each in leveraged bets on a rising ZEC price. Of those, 27 are now losing money, with about $23.7 million in paper losses between them.

It has been revealed that sharp drops have not always lasted. Since January 2025, ZEC has fallen 12% or more in a single day 14 times on Binance. Seven days later, it was higher eight times, with a median gain of 6.5%.

So, why is crypto crashing? A hot inflation report raised the odds of a bigger Fed hike, and ZEC’s leveraged bulls are paying the most for it. A daily close back above $1,050 would be the first sign the selling is easing.

As XRP continues to struggle amid the broad crypto market volatility while failing in multiple attempts to recover, key on-chain metrics are pointing to increased selling pressure among traders.

While momentum remains extremely weak, latest data from crypto analytics platform, Cryptoquant, reveals that sellers have dominated both XRP’s spot and futures markets, putting it at risk of losing the long-held $1 mark.

Per the data, XRP’s cumulative volume delta (CVD) across major cryptocurrency exchanges shows that aggressive selling has dominated both its spot and futures market since September 23.

As of November 12, XRP’s Perpetual CVD on Binance has fallen from -$109 million to about -$1.1 billion. It is important to note that the CVD of an asset is a key metric that measures the difference between the volume of aggressive buy orders and aggressive sell orders over time.

While the metric turns negative when more traders are aggressively selling than buying, the -991 million negative balance in the Binance perpetual CVD signals stronger selling pressure.

With the negative balance on Binance exceeding its previous level by more than 10 times, this indicates that traders have placed significantly more market sell orders than buy orders, either by opening short positions or closing existing long positions.

Apart from its futures market, further data reveals that sellers have also dominated XRP’s spot activity across all major crypto exchanges, including Binance.

Notably, XRP’s All CEX Estimated Spot CVD moved from -$400 million to -$2.9 billion over the same period.

While this marks a $2.5 billion increase in the imbalance favoring sellers, it indicates that XRP spot traders have also been selling XRP more aggressively rather than buying, propelling the asset for further price declines.

#238. DOJ Targets $1.2B in Crypto Stolen From Binance

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5 min read (947 words)
General

DOJ Targets $1.2B in Crypto Stolen From Binance

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read | Sumber: https://bitcoinist.com/doj-targets-1-2b-in-crypto-stolen-from-binance/

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the US Department of Justice DOJ targets the stolen crypto from Binance after it secured court authorization to seize more than $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen during the massive Binance hack in October.
  • The Binance theft, which occurred around October 29, involved more than $6 billion in digital assets, according to the DOJ.
  • The FBI attributed the Binance attack to TraderTraitor, a hacking operation linked to North Korea’s military.

Recent findings suggest that the US Department of Justice DOJ targets the stolen crypto from Binance after it secured court authorization to seize more than $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen during the massive Binance hack in October. The announcement marks a significant development in the recovery effort, as authorities also revealed the disruption of a separate North Korean cybercrime operation that allegedly stole more than $400 million through deepfake-enabled scams.

The Binance theft, which occurred around October 29, involved more than $6 billion in digital assets, according to the DOJ. Government agencies and private-sector partners have since frozen more than $2.7 billion of the stolen funds, with the latest court action covering a portion of that amount.

The FBI attributed the Binance attack to TraderTraitor, a hacking operation linked to North Korea’s military. Investigators say the group stole more than $6 billion in virtual assets before moving the funds through cryptocurrency bridges, mixers, and exchanges in an attempt to obscure their origins.

The DOJ’s latest action allows authorities to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of the stolen cryptocurrency. However, this amount is included in the broader $2.7 billion already frozen through cooperation between US agencies and private companies. It does not represent an additional recovery.

US officials say the government is continuing to trace the remaining assets and coordinate with virtual asset service providers to prevent further movement of the stolen funds.

It has been revealed that binance previously estimated its losses at approximately $6.3 billion and committed company resources to cover the affected assets. On November 12, the exchange said it had completed that process and published an updated proof-of-reserves snapshot.

The DOJ described the recovery effort as a coordinated operation involving its National Security Division, Criminal Division, the FBI, and other law enforcement partners. Officials also emphasized that North Korea has relied on cryptocurrency theft to generate funds for its government and weapons programs.

Alongside the Binance-related enforcement action, the DOJ confirmed that authorities had seized cloud infrastructure used in a separate North Korean hacking campaign known as FaceStealer.

According to the department, the operation has resulted in more than $400 million in cryptocurrency theft over the past 18 months. Rather than relying solely on conventional phishing messages, the attackers used compromised accounts, recorded webcam footage, and AI-generated deepfakes to impersonate people familiar to their targets.

The scheme typically began with an invitation to an online meeting sent through an account previously stolen from another victim. Once the target joined, hackers played prerecorded footage or deepfake videos of people they recognized to establish trust.

The attackers would then introduce a fake technical problem, such as an audio malfunction, and instruct the victim to install software supposedly needed to resolve it. The download instead installed malware that provided access to the victim’s computer, cryptocurrency holdings, and other systems.

In some cases, attackers waited months or even more than a year after the initial compromise before stealing funds or taking control of communication accounts. The FBI also seized more than 900 webcam videos belonging to victims as part of the investigation.

The FaceStealer campaign extended beyond cryptocurrency investors and Web3 professionals. US authorities mentioned the hackers increasingly targeted developers responsible for maintaining open-source software, raising concerns about potential supply-chain attacks.

By compromising a developer’s computer or repository account, attackers could potentially introduce malicious code into software used by other individuals and organizations.

Recent findings suggest that the DOJ said the campaign appeared intended to exploit the trust placed in widely used software and professional relationships. The FBI’s investigation also identified attempts to use compromised accounts and contact lists to approach victims’ colleagues and personal connections.

Sources indicate that the seizure of FaceStealer infrastructure is intended to disrupt the operation and limit the attackers’ ability to continue targeting cryptocurrency owners and software developers. The FBI has also published guidance to help potential victims identify the scheme and respond to possible compromises.

Recent findings suggest that the two enforcement actions highlight the growing scale and sophistication of North Korean-linked cybercrime targeting the digital asset industry. While the Binance case demonstrates the financial impact of large-scale exchange breaches, FaceStealer illustrates how social engineering and deepfake technology can expose individuals and organizations to substantial losses.

Recent findings suggest that the recovery of the Binance funds also highlights the importance of cooperation between law enforcement agencies, exchanges, blockchain analytics firms, and other crypto service providers. However, freezing stolen assets does not automatically mean they have been returned to their rightful owners. Further legal proceedings and asset-tracing efforts remain necessary.

With more than $1.2 billion now covered by court-authorized seizure or restraint orders, US authorities have taken another step toward recovering funds connected to one of the largest cryptocurrency thefts on record. Meanwhile, the disruption of FaceStealer signals that investigators are also focusing on the techniques used to compromise individuals before funds are stolen.

Do you think the DOJ’s latest actions will make it harder for North Korean hackers to target cryptocurrency exchanges?

Could the growing use of AI-generated deepfakes make social engineering one of the biggest security threats facing the crypto industry?

Who Is Colette Kress, Jensen Huang’s Successor as Nvidia CEO?

Who Is Colette Kress, Jensen Huang’s Successor as Nvidia CEO?

According to recent reports, for the first time in 33 years, someone other than Jensen Huang is running Nvidia. And the person taking over is not an engineer, a chip designer, or a Silicon Valley founder.

Colette Kress, Nvidia's 59-year-old chief financial officer, was named interim CEO Thursday following Huang's abrupt resignation amid reports of extramarital affairs and allegations involving a suspected Chinese intelligence operative.

Kress will remain CFO while the board searches for a permanent replacement, according to Nvidia's regulatory filing. She inherits a manufacturer worth trillions of dollars, a shaken investor base, and a management structure built around one man.

In a recent development, kress joined Nvidia in September 2013, when it was primarily known for graphics cards used in video games. She arrived with nearly 25 years of financial experience across some of America's largest technology companies.

She spent eight years at Texas Instruments before joining Microsoft in 1997. During her 13-year tenure there, she became CFO of the Server and Tools division, overseeing financial strategy for Microsoft's enterprise computing business.

In 2010, she moved to Cisco as senior vice president and CFO of its Business Technology and Operations Finance organization, managing financial planning and business development across the networking giant's operations.

Kress holds a finance degree from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University, according to her official biography.

Sources indicate that her move to Nvidia came with an unusual endorsement. Her two sons, then enthusiastic gamers, encouraged her to join the company responsible for the graphics chips powering their favorite games, according to Forbes.

Huang personally recruited her, explaining his vision for AI computing on a whiteboard during their discussions, Wired reported. At the time, Nvidia was the smallest tech giant Kress had worked for.

When Kress joined Nvidia, its annual revenue stood at approximately $4.13 billion. By fiscal 2026, that figure had reached $215.9 billion, an increase of more than 50 times.

Huang drove Nvidia's technological strategy, but Kress oversaw the finances supporting its expansion from gaming hardware into data centers and AI infrastructure.

Her tenure included Nvidia's $6.9 billion acquisition of networking specialist Mellanox and an increasingly aggressive strategy of investing in companies that purchase its computing hardware.

Those relationships now include CoreWeave, in which Nvidia invested another $2 billion in January. CoreWeave's rapid growth reflects enormous demand for Nvidia-powered computing, alongside the financial costs of building that infrastructure.

Kress also became Nvidia's principal financial voice to Wall Street, regularly explaining margins, chip demand and revenue forecasts during earnings calls.

Forbes ranked her among America's richest self-made women in 2026, with almost $750 million in Nvidia shares as of Wednesday's close.

Industry observers note that kress takes charge as Nvidia faces questions about the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending. Nvidia had already lost approximately $1.27 trillion in market value from its October peak before the board publicly revealed its investigation on Huang’s love affairs.

She must also navigate Washington's restrictions on advanced chip exports to China and scrutiny surrounding Nvidia's commercial relationships. The board has noted it has no reason to believe company secrets or U.S. national security were compromised in the allegations involving Huang.

According to recent reports, her financial expertise cannot entirely replace Huang's technical background or his personal relationships with developers, customers, and governments. Maintaining Nvidia's engineering leadership will require close coordination with the executives responsible for its chips and software.

Kress has promised to build on Huang's legacy, saying that “Nvidia's strength has always come from its people.”.

It has been revealed that her first major public test arrives Tuesday, November 17, when Nvidia reports its third-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings. The company has scheduled its results for approximately 1:20 p.m. Pacific, followed by an investor call at 2 p.m.

North Korean hackers launch memecoins to launder funds stolen in the Binance hack, while xStocks intends to add hundreds of Hong Kong-listed equities in the coming weeks.

North Korean hackers created memecoins to launder cryptocurrency stolen in the $6.3 billion Binance hack, according to a report from blockchain analytics firm Elliptic.Between Nov. 5 and 7, the hackers created at least six tokens on NEAR and used liquidity pools on decentralized exchanges to move $430,000 of stolen funds between wallets, Elliptic stated. However, the tokens attracted almost no outside trading and were abandoned shortly after launch.

Elliptic said the same laundering technique was also used following the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in 2025, when North Korean-linked actors moved at least $24 million through a newly created token on the TRON blockchain.

Sources indicate that payward said the latest expansion brings xStocks’ offering to more than 1,500 tokenized assets. The company reported more than $45 billion in cumulative transaction volume and over 550,000 unique holders.

Payward said it prepares to add hundreds of Hong Kong-listed equities in the coming weeks.

South Korea’s Financial Services Commission (FSC) looks to allow crypto exchanges to suspend deposits and withdrawals when hacking is suspected, rather than waiting until a breach is confirmed.

The FSC remarked it would issue a no-action letter permitting preventive suspensions under certain conditions. Current rules prohibit exchanges from blocking withdrawals without legitimate grounds and explicitly allow restrictions only when a hacking incident is clearly established.

The regulator also called for round-the-clock monitoring and incident response, higher cold-wallet holdings, and stronger insurance coverage and reserves.

South Korean crypto exchange GOPAX declared on November 6 it was suspending trading, deposits and withdrawals and moving all user assets to cold wallets. The firm had received threatening emails that claimed a hack was imminent, and took the drastic step of putting everything on ice on the recommendation of financial authorities.

Nomura has held talks with potential buyers, including Marex Group but is yet to make a final decision and could keep the business.

Thailand’s securities regulator has proposed capping daily stablecoin deposits and withdrawals at 5 million baht ($148,000) each per customer at regulated crypto operators.

Sources indicate that the limit would apply separately to deposits and withdrawals at each operator, Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) remarked in a Thursday announcement. The regulator said the rules aim to curb money laundering, cybercrime and attempts to bypass cross-border money transfer rules.

The draft would bar stablecoin transfers to and from third-party wallets.

Sources indicate that thailand’s SEC will block access to Bitget from December 5. It has also proposed fresh tests for retail investors before allowing them to invest in ICOs. The tests would require knowledge of at least six areas including digital tokens and investor rights, blockchain technology, digital-asset wallets and distribution channels. The proposals will be up for comment until November 25. The SEC is also seeking feedback on new rules around margin loans and ETFs, but has ruled out allowing leveraged or crypto ETFs at this stage.

South Korean crypto firm Bithumb Asset, has invested $85 million into a luxury resort project in Hoi An in Vietnam being built by local real estate developer Asia Estate. Kraken’s parent Payward is increasingly relying on businesses outside crypto trading to support its financial performance as weaker market activity weighs on transaction fees.

The company reported $487 million in total platform margin for the third quarter of 2026, representing a 12% decline from the same period last year. However, its expanding financial services operations helped offset some of the pressure, with revenue connected to client assets and access to products, data, and services accounting for a larger share of its business.

Payward also reported signs of improvement compared with the previous quarter, as total platform margin increased 12% and adjusted earnings recovered alongside a pickup in trading activity.

The third-quarter results reflect the challenges facing cryptocurrency exchanges as lower trading activity puts pressure on businesses that depend heavily on transaction fees.

Payward’s total platform margin reached $487 million, down 12% year over year. The firm uses this metric instead of adjusted revenue, deducting trading costs and staking rewards paid to customers.

In a recent development, the decline comes amid similar difficulties across the exchange industry. Coinbase reported a 35% year-over-year drop in third-quarter revenue, while Gemini Space Station recorded a 19% decline in revenue alongside a 73% fall in trading volumes.

These figures highlight why major crypto platforms are increasingly looking for ways to diversify their income rather than depend almost entirely on market activity and trading fees.

Payward’s expansion into financial services appears to be helping soften the impact of weaker cryptocurrency trading.

Income linked to client assets and access to products, data, and services accounted for 52% of the firm’s total platform margin in the third quarter, compared with 46% during the same period last year. The company has been developing several business lines beyond its core exchange operations, including banking, asset management, and Payward Services, which provides financial infrastructure to other businesses.

According to recent reports, its strategy also extends into traditional futures, equities, tokenized stocks, payments, custody, and lending. By broadening its offering, Payward aims to generate revenue from a wider range of financial activities, reducing its exposure to fluctuations in cryptocurrency trading volumes.

Sources indicate that the company has also identified artificial intelligence as a fifth business pillar. Its intends include developing a personal finance agent and investment funds connected to its xStocks tokenized equities platform.

Payward’s broader financial strategy also includes investments and discussions with established financial institutions.

In November, a fund affiliated with Payward and its clients purchased an undisclosed amount of AAVE tokens through secondary-market transactions. The move followed earlier discussions between the company and decentralized lending platform Aave about potential areas of cooperation.

The investment reflects Payward’s growing interest in decentralized finance and asset management, alongside its existing exchange and infrastructure operations. The tech giant has also explored partnerships with major banks. Payward reportedly held discussions with Wells Fargo about providing liquidity for cryptocurrency trading. Separate talks with BNY focused on a potential financial infrastructure partnership involving digital assets, custody, wealth management, trading, and payments.

These initiatives could help Payward strengthen its position in both traditional finance and the digital asset industry, although the discussions do not necessarily mean that formal agreements have been reached.

Although third-quarter performance remained below year-earlier levels, the latest figures indicate that Payward’s business improved compared with the second quarter.

Total platform margin increased 12% quarter over quarter, while adjusted earnings also moved higher as cryptocurrency trading activity recovered and income from client assets and services expanded.

Industry observers note that the improvement suggests that Payward’s diversification strategy is beginning to provide additional support during periods of weaker market activity. However, the annual revenue decline indicates that the firm’s core trading business remains exposed to broader cryptocurrency market conditions.

For Payward, the next challenge will be turning its growing range of financial services into a more consistent source of income while maintaining its position in the competitive crypto exchange market.

Pushed an patch to quickly address BTC swap/send concerns while using "Classic Wallet" before we release the full v3.1.2 this weekend Simply close / reopen the app and you should see: 3.1.1-652.1 or 3.1.1-652.2 in the "About MyDoge" settings.

In Dogecoin ecosystem news, DogeOS is nearing mainnet launch, bringing an EVM-compatible app layer to DOGE that would let developers build DeFi, games and other apps on Dogecoin for the first time.

In October, DogeOS opened a public test network for Ethereum-style trading, lending and other applications using DOGE, seeking to give Dogecoin holders more ways to use their coins beyond payments and price speculation.

In a recent post on X, Dogecoin Foundation director of product Timothy Stebbing shared a Dogecoin ecosystem 2026 enhancement.

Stebbing predicts that the next three to four years for Dogecoin are likely to be shaped more by the development and adoption of smart-contract application layers than by large, pre-emptive changes to Dogecoin’s base protocol. He cited DogeOS as an early and visible example of that direction. If it and similar efforts succeed in attracting sustained developer activity and real usage while continuing to treat Dogecoin as the settlement and value-transfer foundation, Stebbing sees the ecosystem gaining additional utility without compromising the simplicity and reliability of the Layer 1.

However, the proposed mechanism for native proof verification on Dogecoin still requires community discussion and, ultimately, activation. Thus, adoption will depend on whether the resulting applications are useful enough that people choose to use them. None of these uncertainties change the underlying architectural advantage: the Layer 1 can remain a focused means of exchange while the surrounding ecosystem gains the capacity for richer functionality.
